assertion_audit.fails_if: The lift store resolves outside either fixture home, or the new grant CLI option is absent/refused; line 67 is only a setup check, not a real-store postcondition.

The unlifted 95% dispatch is admitted, a valid project grant is ignored, its reserve release is lost, future sessions lose the governing grant, or another project inherits it; restoring return True for project scopes reddens line 149 in negative-control.log.

Newest grant replaces scope precedence, another project inherits the project grant, or session scope fails to outrank a newer project grant; comparisons use independent persisted grant IDs, not an expected scope handed to the resolver.

Repeated project options collapse records, reasons diverge, either project loses coverage, listing loses a project scope, clear changes the wrong scope or fails to revoke, or a repeat clear is not a no-op.
A clear for an absent project lift revokes the global fallback or reports it as cleared.
Project credits are not selected, sessions receive separate cap semantics, a pre-cap account balance is held, the full cap is admitted, or a different project spends the lift.
The watch sweep loses the matching project, emits the lift to the other project, produces duplicate rows, changes lift identity, wrongly session-scopes project delivery, or loses the end transition.
Conflicting scope flags are accepted, fail for an unrelated reason, or write a lift before refusal.

Existing --check --project parsing stops forwarding its argument to the report owner or --for-project is silently accepted outside --lift; the fake report return is not itself asserted as proof of behavior.

The real picker path is not reached, the lifted lane is excluded, CLI dispatch fails, or the selected backend differs; restoring project=None at the picker budget-block boundary removes the sole candidate and reddens line 335.
